raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Third of four stacked PRs split out of #35335. Base: the planner library. This layer is the **runtime wiring** that turns a plan into a placement.

## Flow

`server_warmup.maybe_apply_auto_residency` runs between the synthetic warmup and the ready signal: **apply → re-warm → validate → (rollback)**. `GPUWorker.apply_auto_residency` builds the rank report from the warmup records, plans jointly across ranks, applies the changes transactionally (`apply_residency_changes` / `commit_residency_changes` / `rollback_residency_changes`), and the validation re-warm rolls the round back on a memory shortfall or a materially slower probe. `rollback_auto_residency` restores the last calibrated placement. The scheduler and both scheduler clients fan the `AutoResidencyReq` control request out to every replica and merge the outcomes (a failed rollback wins over an adjusted replica).

## Mechanisms it needs

- **Layerwise offload:** per-group resident layouts and pin frontiers, host-store repacking, disable/enable offload for promotions, and release of host stores once a resident placement is validated.
- **ServerArgs:** auto residency modes next to the explicit ones (`configured_residency_mode` vs runtime `auto_residency_mode`, the shared `host_pin_budget`); `auto_tune` excludes fixed loading paths (quantized, direct GPU, LTX-2 original) per component; quantized component offload capability is enforced at load (`supports_quantized_component_offload`).
- The post-request residency hint reuses the planner's candidate ranking.
- `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_AUTO_RESIDENCY` is the kill switch (defined in the measurement layer, honored by the gate).

## Tests

`test_auto_residency_warmup` (apply / validate / rollback rounds, replica merge), `test_layerwise_offload`, `test_health_warmup_gate`, `test_server_args`, `test_dp_routing`, `test_transformer_quant`, and the apply-side tests in `test_auto_residency`. 748 tests pass on this layer.

## Stack

1. #37916 — measurement and record types
2. #37917 — planner as a pure library
3. #37918 — apply / validate / rollback wiring
4. #35335 — per-pipeline containment fixes and CI baselines

Every layer's tree is a prefix of #35335's; the union is byte-identical to the original branch merged with main.

---

<!-- pr-states:end -->

## Regression fixes (2026-09-07)

Comparing this head against main's run [34015151838](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34015151838) on the same H100 runners showed three default-command cases serving slower: `fast_hunyuan_video` 9.2 s → 10.2–12.9 s, `lingbot_video_moe_t2v` 6.6 s → 8.0–8.4 s, `hunyuanvideo_modelopt_fp8_t2v` 2.6 s → 6.9–10.1 s (the last two had no e2e baseline; #38335 adds them). Commit `1e29438` fixes the causes, each reproduced on an H200 devbox with 80 GiB of free VRAM emulated:

| case | main | this PR before | this PR after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fast_hunyuan_video | 9.77 s | 10.16 s | 9.08 s |
| hunyuanvideo_modelopt_fp8_t2v | 2.43 s | 6.84 s | 2.24 s |
| lingbot_video_moe_t2v | 6.38 s | 7.60 s | 4.21 s |

- `ServerArgsAutoTuner` no longer skips main's memory-threshold placement under server warmup. Calibration starts from that placement and refines it; it never serves below it when a promotion is declined.
- The probe fit subtracts the weight floor the planner already uses (resident components plus the largest streamed one), so a streamed 24 GiB DiT is no longer extrapolated as activations (77 GiB estimate for a 33 GiB request).
- `finalize_resident_layerwise_placement` only empties the host caching allocator when the freed pinned stores exceed 1 GiB. Dropping it after a 0.1 GiB VAE promotion discarded the pinned blocks component-offload text encoders recycle for their per-request D2H copy, so the next request re-pinned 8–14 GiB synchronously (3.5–4.8 s).
- `TimestepPreparationStage` logs the timesteps' shape instead of the tensor, which forced a device sync behind the DiT prefetch (158 ms vs 0.6 ms).


**Follow-ups (2026-09-08).** `5cb56be` keys the MiniMax-H3 VAE decode-dtype store by module layout: the runtimes on shared CI runners expose different parameter sets (144 vs 288 tensors) and were deleting each other's store, which left the decoder weights in anonymous host memory and made the 2-GPU ref2va decode 12.9 s instead of 2.3 s. `5cb99db` refreshes the allocated/reserved peak guards of the 29 H100 and 4 RTX 5090 cases whose text encoders or VAEs the planner now keeps resident, plus the warmup peak of `wan2_2_t2v_a14b_2gpu` and the sampled steps of two cases; no e2e expectation changed.

A full per-case comparison of this head against main's run 34015151838 (46 single-GPU, 28 two-GPU, 6 RTX 5090 and 5 B200 cases) shows every case equal or faster within main's own run-to-run noise (up to 1.08 on single samples). The B200 nvfp4 cases look 1.6-1.9x slower on some runs, but that tracks the runner node, not the branch: `b200-cirrascale1-*` and `b200-di01-*` run `qwen_image_2512_modelopt_nvfp4_t2i` at 331-359 ms/step for every branch including unrelated PRs, `b200-fin03-*` at 187-213 ms/step for main and for #37811; a B200 devbox gives 177 ms/step for both main and this head.

@@ -89,7 +89,7 @@ Use `sglang generate --help` and `sglang serve --help` for the full argument lis
 - `--lora-merge-mode {auto|merge|dynamic}`: choose how LoRA is applied. `auto` normally merges regular weights, but keeps FSDP-sharded weights dynamic to avoid full-gather peaks. For a single adapter, it also stays dynamic when an estimate shows that merging would round away more than 50% of the update's norm. `merge` forces merging; `dynamic` applies the adapter at forward time.
 - `--num-gpus {N}`: number of GPUs to use
 - `--numa-node {N} [N ...]`: NUMA node for each GPU worker, the i-th value for the worker on local GPU i. When unset, each worker binds its CPUs and host memory to its GPU's NUMA node on multi-socket hosts, as srt does (CPUs only without `CAP_SYS_NICE`); set `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` to turn that off. Unbound workers on a two-socket host (e.g. GB200/GB300) can drift to the other socket, which slows host-bound steps and makes latency vary run to run.
-- `--performance-mode {manual|auto|speed|memory}` / `--mode`: preset for latency/throughput and memory defaults. `auto` is the default and dispatches residency from selected-GPU headroom and workload type: image DiTs stay resident above the 45 GiB threshold, while video DiT placement remains model-specific. It uses FSDP only for validated DiT-offload replacement paths. `speed` keeps `torch.compile` disabled unless a model-specific deployment config opts in after validation; pass `--enable-torch-compile true` to enable it explicitly. Use `manual` to keep performance-related server args under explicit user control. Explicit offload, FSDP, and parallelism flags take precedence in all modes.
+- `--performance-mode {manual|auto|speed|memory}` / `--mode`: preset for latency/throughput and memory defaults. `auto` is the default. With an eligible synthetic server warmup, it starts from a load-safe placement, measures the representative workload, and jointly selects component/layer residency against every rank and execution-phase VRAM constraint plus HostPin limits. These are simultaneous constraints on one placement decision, not independently spendable budgets. Warmup also observes each declared layer group's call count, so repeated groups can receive independent resident-layer allocations while one-shot or unused groups use HostPin or whole-component residency instead. Multi-process HostPin planning stays inside non-overlapping per-worker shares. Explicit/online quantization and direct GPU loading fix only their affected components; eligible encoders, VAEs, and other components in the same pipeline still participate. The selected placement targets the model-default (or `--warmup-sampling-params`) workload; use representative warmup parameters or explicit residency for larger production shapes, batches, or output counts. Candidate planning keeps each rank within the allocated-memory peaks of its first successful calibration and each execution phase, so extra card capacity is not spent on larger resident sets. Both serving phases and placement transitions respect this limit, and post-placement validation cannot raise it. The separate card-capacity reserve still checks allocator-reserved memory so the selected layout retains request headroom. Pipelines that cannot preserve their numerical path across a runtime residency change keep their static placement. Layerwise prefetch depth and residency policy remain explicit because their latency effect depends on runtime overlap rather than weight size alone. Offline, realtime, and no-warmup paths retain the model/card fallback policy. It uses FSDP only for validated DiT-offload replacement paths. `speed` keeps `torch.compile` disabled unless a model-specific deployment config opts in after validation; pass `--enable-torch-compile true` to enable it explicitly. Use `manual` to keep performance-related server args under explicit user control. Explicit offload, FSDP, and parallelism flags take precedence in all modes.
 - `--direct-gpu-weight-loading {true|false}`: opt into direct GPU loading for an unquantized, GPU-resident, TP=1 DiT by materializing its complete checkpoint state dict on GPU. Compatible tensors become parameter storage without another GPU copy, while tensors requiring transforms can still need temporary allocations. It is disabled by default; startup time and peak GPU memory remain model-dependent, so benchmark the target model before deployment. It is incompatible with DiT CPU/layerwise offload and FSDP.
 - `--tp-size {N}`: tensor parallelism size. Depending on the pipeline, it can shard the DiT, one or more encoders, or both.
 - `--sp-degree {N}`: sequence parallelism size
@@ -99,6 +99,7 @@ Use `sglang generate --help` and `sglang serve --help` for the full argument lis
 - `--enable-cfg-parallel {true|false}`: enable or explicitly disable CFG parallelism. Requests that disable CFG remain valid on a CFG-parallel server, but extra CFG ranks redundantly recompute the single active branch.
 - `--encoder-parallel {auto|fold|dp|replicate}`: how native encoders use the GPUs in each DiT replica. `auto` TP-folds a native text/image encoder wide enough to benefit, selects batch DP for an explicitly supported native text encoder when it can engage, and otherwise keeps the existing encoder TP layout; `fold` shards native text/image encoders across the full replica whenever dimensions allow; `dp` splits a batched encode across supported native text encoder copies and composes with encoder TP; `replicate` disables folding and batch DP. Encoder collectives never cross `--dp-size` replicas. See [Encoder Parallelism](/docs/sglang-diffusion/encoder_parallel).
 - `--warmup-mode {off|request|server}`: control startup warmup for `sglang serve`; `off` skips warmup, `request` primes the request path, and `server` runs a full synthetic server warmup before serving traffic
+- `--warmup-sampling-params JSON`: override the representative width, height, frame count, inference steps, or guidance values used by synthetic warmup and automatic residency planning. The warmup still caps executed steps and large video probes; the uncapped values describe the workload the memory planner must fit.
 - `--enable-torch-compile {true|false}`: compile native diffusion hot paths. When no warmup mode is configured, this also enables server warmup so first real requests do not pay compile latency.
 - `--offload-during-compile {true|false}`: when compile warmup is active, temporarily layerwise-offload DiT weights and move resident non-DiT components off-device so `max-autotune` fits on tighter-memory GPUs; the configured serving residency is restored before real traffic. Skipped under existing layerwise offload, Cache-DiT, or FSDP.
 - `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph {true|false}`: capture supported DiT forwards as breakable CUDA graph segments to reduce launch overhead. Each served shape is captured separately at warmup: pass every served resolution in `--warmup-resolutions` (and the frame count in `--warmup-num-frames` for video), otherwise only the model default shape is captured and other shapes run eager. Unset, it is on for `LTX2TwoStagePipeline` on LTX-2/LTX-2.3 when CUDA serving on GPUs with at least 130 GiB keeps the DiTs resident (server warmup; no torch.compile, Cache-DiT, batching, or `--lora-path`; LTX-2.3 in `resident` mode, its default on those GPUs). On a model outside the validated list it stays enabled with a warning; compare outputs against eager. If the startup warmup captures no graph (the model's denoising stage does not use BCG), the server warns that it runs eager. An `lossless` or `high` request is rejected when it would mount request-scoped DiT fusions that were not present during lossless graph capture; VAE-only request-gated paths remain compatible.

@@ -123,7 +123,7 @@ See [OpenAI API: Served model name](/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/openai_api#served `auto` - Default. Keeps every component resident when the least-free GPU has at least twice the model's per-GPU weights free (sized from the cached checkpoint; not with batching or on shared-memory devices). Otherwise keeps legacy safe offload defaults and uses FSDP/CFG only on validated multi-GPU deployments where FSDP can replace DiT offload. + Default. A future continuous value such as `0.0` to `1.0` could express the speed-memory tradeoff more precisely, but it would need model-specific memory models and clearer user expectations. Until then, use the preset plus explicit flags for overrides. +The calibrated planner is exact for the candidate states and memory constraints it receives, but transfer-based latency estimates cannot model every prefetch overlap or bandwidth interaction. +            if not isinstance(module, LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin):
+                continue
